title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the 1986 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs, in which Grothendieck axiomatizes a combinatorial, 'tame' (modérée) topology. The basic object M (an 'm-gérie', reading uncertain) is a set of 'cells' or 'pieces' carrying several relations:
- ≤ : inclusion;
- ≪ : something like 'X lies in the closure, or is a face, of Y';
- °≪ : a strict or immediate version of ≪;
- |·| : support.
Other notions on these pages: 'figures' Fig(M), which are closed, normalized finite configurations F̃ such as the closure of a cell together with its faces; Ss(F), the ordered set of sub-cells of a figure.

The previous page (p.56) tried to define homomorphisms f : F → F' between broader structures. Grothendieck found that requiring an order isomorphism on sub-cells (**) forces elementary figures to go to elementary ones, i.e. f_U : U → U'. He judged the competing non-U-preserving example (ex. B, p.50) 'hétéroclite' and unappealing for dimension reasons.

This page. He returns to the restricted notion f_M = f : M → M' of pp.27–28. For every normalized figure F̃ ∈ Fig(M), with F' = f(F), the restriction f|F̃ : F̃ → F̃' is an isomorphism, presumably of ordered sets. Hence condition (**) holds and all the corollaries of pp.28–29 are available.

In modern terms, f is a cellular map that is an isomorphism on each closed cell, i.e. on each lower set of the face poset. Such maps are 'locally embeddings' but not globally: they are like the realization map from a Δ-complex or semi-simplicial set to its image, or a covering-type/folding map of regular cell complexes. Grothendieck accordingly remarks that f is close to an embedding but need not be injective. His example: M quasi-ensembliste and not connected (reading uncertain), with the canonical homomorphism M → Figures(L).

He then asks: when f is injective, can M be identified with a sub-structure of M', i.e. is M isomorphic to its image with the induced structure? Since compatibility with ≤ was arranged earlier, the issue is the face relation. Given f(X) °≪ Y' ≤ f(Y) in M', must Y' be of the form f(Y₁), with moreover X °≪ Y₁ ≤ Y in M? This is the familiar distinction between an injective morphism and an embedding (full, relation-reflecting sub-object).

The next page settles it under the extra hypothesis that f reflects ≪: f(X) ≪ f(Y) ⇒ X ≪ Y. Under that hypothesis, with f injective, Y' = f(Y₁) and °≪ is induced by ≪. He then turns to classifying homomorphisms M → Figures(P) for a set P, through the support map X ↦ |X|.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The non-injectivity example is only sketched and its hypotheses are partly illegible, so it cannot be checked. The embedding question is left open here; it is answered on p.58 only under an added reflection hypothesis, which Grothendieck himself presumes is not automatic.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms of cell-structures that restrict to isomorphisms on every closed figure (closed cell with its faces)
ideas.modern_name: cellular maps that are isomorphisms on closed cells / maps of face posets that are isomorphisms on lower sets (as in realization of Δ-complexes, semi-simplicial sets, regular CW posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore of combinatorial topology (Eilenberg–Zilber for semi-simplicial complexes; Björner and others for regular CW posets)

ideas.what: Such maps resemble embeddings but are not injective in general
ideas.modern_name: local embedding vs. global embedding (e.g. Δ-complex versus simplicial complex)

ideas.what: When is an injective homomorphism an identification with a sub-structure? Requires reflecting the face relation ≪ / °≪
ideas.modern_name: embedding = injective + relation-reflecting (full/induced substructure, strong monomorphism)

ideas.what: Axiomatic framework of 'm-géries' with relations ≤, ≪, °≪, |·| and figures, as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology; compare o-minimal cell decompositions and face posets of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimality, 1980s–98); Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme (Esquisse, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces tame topology in general terms; the m-gérie formalism itself appears unpublished

missed.claim: An open question in the axiomatic tame-topology formalism: does an injective homomorphism of m-géries identify M with a sub-m-gérie of M' (Y' = f(Y₁) with X °≪ Y₁ ≤ Y)? It is resolved on the next page only under an extra reflection hypothesis, and the general case is left open.
missed.quote: f(X) °≪ Y' ≤ f(Y) dans M' / est-ce que Y' est de la forme f(Y₁) ? / On voudrait de plus, bien sûr X °≪ Y₁ ≤ Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of minor interest. It belongs to the largely unexplored 1986 axiomatization of tame topology, which could be compared with face-poset and exit-path descriptions of stratified spaces. The specific question, however, is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries routine foundational bookkeeping for Grothendieck's unpublished 'Analysis situs' formalism: maps that are isomorphisms on closed cells need not be injective, and he asks when an injective one is an embedding. The overall framework is unpublished and of historical interest, but this page has no result a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Revenons finalement pour retomber sur' (OK).
After f|F̃ : F̃ ≅ F̃' the superscript note likely reads 'isom. d'ens. ordonnés' (cf. p.56 (**)) rather than 'donc d'une relation'.
'pour [-tout-]' is plausibly 'pour tout' with a crossed word; '(figure normalisée au sens général)' is uncertain.
Corollaries are of 'p. 28, 29' (the image shows 'des p. 28, 29').
The crossed underlined word before 'identifier' looks like 'sous-catégories' or 'sous-ensemblistes'. The next line reads roughly 'M' ! i.e. ... sont-elles une sous- ...; et M y est-il isomorphe'.
